reason: The passage depicts Joseph as a leader who exercises authority and tests his brothers through stern interrogation and imprisonment rather than demonstrating humility in the face of their concerns. Joseph speaks harshly (קָשׁוֹת) to his brothers, accuses them of espionage, and maintains his position of power throughout most of the encounter. While Joseph eventually shows emotional vulnerability (crying) and acknowledges divine providence, this occurs after his brothers have already demonstrated humility before him, not in response to criticism directed at Joseph himself. The brothers and Judah display humility in their subordinate positions, but Joseph as the leader does not model humility in the face of challenge or criticism. His leadership is characterized by the exercise of power and testing of others rather than by receptiveness to criticism or humble deference.
